headline: Govt orders shops and malls to close by 8pm nationwide
summary: The move aims to save electricity and improve power management across the country.
details: The government has directed all shopping malls, markets, and shops across Bangladesh to close by 8:00 PM to save electricity and improve power management.
A memo issued by the Coordination-2 branch of the Power Division on Wednesday night outlined the new regulations.
Under the new rules, shopping malls, markets, and shops can remain open from 11:00 AM to 8:00 PM.
Additionally, all illuminated billboards must be turned off by 7:00 PM, and all decorative lighting must be completely shut down.
The directive also applies to ongoing and upcoming fairs, trade fairs, and cultural programs, which must now end by 8:00 PM.
Essential services, including food shops, hospitals, and pharmacies, are exempt from these restrictions.
This decision reduces the previous closing time of 9:00 PM, which had been in effect since June 11, by one hour.

headline_marked: 6 [[senior police officers suspended]] for prolonged absence
headline: 6 senior police officers suspended for prolonged absence
summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs has suspended six high-ranking officials, including Additional DIGs, for remaining absent from duty without permission.
details: The government has suspended six senior police officials for remaining absent from their duty for an extended period without leave or prior permission.

The suspended officers include Additional DIGs Biplob Kumar Sarkar and Sudip Kumar Chakrabarty, SP Md Iqbal Hossain, SP Kazi Ashraful Azim, Additional SP Rajan Kumar Das, and DMP Assistant Commissioner Golam Ruhani.
According to the Ministry of Home Affairs, the officials were served notices asking them to explain their unauthorised absence, but none of them replied.
Departmental proceedings later found prima facie evidence of misconduct, leading to their suspension under the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 2018.
The suspension orders, issued via separate notifications today, have taken immediate effect.
caption:
